Build succeeds. The audit log confirms the new format: `customerCode=NSW-16E6609E`.

## Summary

I redesigned owner identity so `customerCode` is now `<REGION>-<HASH8>`, touching three files with minimal, cohesive changes:

**`CustomerCode.java`** — rewrote `assign` to take the `Owner` and return `Locality.of(city, postcode) + "-" + hash8(telephone + lastName)`, where `hash8` yields the first 8 upper-case hex chars of SHA-256. Dropped the per-city sequence entirely. Added a small `region(customerCode)` helper so downstream code can source the region from the identity itself. The SHA logic lives in tiny new methods (`hash8`, `sha256`), keeping every function simple.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — one line: `CustomerCode.assign(owner)` (the postcode-derived region and normalized E.164 telephone are already on the owner at that point).

**`OwnerMapper.java`** — one line: `locality` now derives from `CustomerCode.region(owner.getCustomerCode())` instead of an independent `Locality.of(...)` call, moving it onto the new identity.

The membership number, check digit, and audit record all reference `owner.getCustomerCode()` already, so they automatically follow the new identity with no further edits. Test suite is green (1/1, BUILD SUCCESS).
